title: Gravitational Wavefunction Collapse (Schrödinger cells, Black Holes)
author: Dr Logic
rules:
If you are familiar with the ruleset, this puzzle is a 3* at maximum. Before solving I recommend the below puzzles as a warm up.

This is the fourth in a series of puzzles featuring this ruleset, play the others here:

•
Supermassive Black Holes (★) (I)

•
Black Holes and Revelations (★★★) (II)

•
Spaghettification ((★★★★)) (III)

Let me know what you thought of this puzzle in the comments!

Happy solving!

Dr Logic

Rules:

• Normal Quantum Sudoku rules apply, place the digits 0-9 once each in every row, column and marked 3x3 box.

• Schrödinger cells: Exactly one cell in every row, column and region is a Schrödinger cell, and it contains two different digits, its states. For the purpose of constraints, the value of a Schrödinger cell is the sum of its states. Given digits are not Schrödinger cells.

• Black Holes: Place four 3×3 black holes inside the grid. The centre of each is its singularity, and the eight surrounding cells form its accretion disk. Black holes may not overlap or touch orthogonally, and no two singularities may share a row or column. In this puzzle, due to the quantum effects, singularities are unconstrained in value. A singularity may be a Schrödinger cell.

• Accretion disk lines: Each accretion disk carries exactly one of the following lines, and each type is used by exactly one disk: Region Sum, Dutch Whispers, Parity, Renban. The black hole associated with the Parity line has a broken singularity, the digit on the singularity is unconstrained in size.

• Gravity arrows: A cell containing arrows contains a value equal to the cumulative number of cells on black holes (singularity or accretion disk) among the cells the arrows point through, from the adjacent cell to the edge of the grid. Arrows may point in any of the eight directions, and an arrow cell may be a Schrödinger cell. Arrows cannot be placed on black holes.

• White dwarfs: A white dot between two cells means their values are consecutive.

• Red dwarfs: A red dot between two cells means their values are in a 1:2 ratio.

• Moons: A digit in a grey circle is a given. It must be low (1-4) if the cell is not on an accretion disk, and high (5-9) if it is. No moon may be on a singularity.

Standard constraint rules:

• Region Sum: Region borders divide the line into segments, and every segment has the same sum of values. The line must pass through more than one region.

• Renban: Values on a renban form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits.

• German Whispers: Adjacent cells on the line differ in value by at least 5.

• Parity: Adjacent cells on the line have values of different parity.

Play 'Gravitational Wavefunction Collapse'
solutionCode: The digits on the renban accretion disk, read clockwise from the top-left cell, with brackets flanking both states of any S-cells on the line. E.G: 123456(78)9
